title: QwenLM/qwen-code
text: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal. https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/overview The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat. 中文 | Deutsch | français | 日本語 | Русский | Português (Brasil) | 한국어 Qwen Code 1.0 Preview Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together the agent harness capabilities of Qoder and Qwen Code in an open-source release. Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview · Documentation · 中文文档. Why Qwen Code? Agentic out of the box — Auto-Memory, Skills, SubAgents, and MCP work from the first session. Agent Teams, Agent Arena, and Dynamic Workflows are built in too — experimental or opt-in, as noted in Capabilities. Open-source, inside and out — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. Multi-protocol — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. Beyond the terminal — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / WeCom / Feishu and more). Tip Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI. Installation Looking for Qwen Code 1.0 Preview? Get started here. The instructions below are for the main version. Linux / macOS: curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash Windows: irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect. NPM / Homebrew NPM (requires Node.js 22+): npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest Homebrew (macOS / Linux): brew install qwen-code Quick Start Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code: cd /path/to/your-project qwen Inside the session, run /auth and choose Qwen Account with Subscription to sign in with your Plus or Pro subscription, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try: Explain this repository and show me where to start. See the Authentication Guide and Settings Reference for detailed setup. See the terminal interface How to Use Qwen Code Choose the interface that fits your workflow: Interface Get started Terminal Run qwen in your project — see Quick Start. Desktop Download Qwen Code Desktop for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Web Run qwen serve --open to open the Web UI in your browser. (experimental) Editor Set up VS Code, Zed, or JetBrains. Chat Connect Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, WeCom, Feishu, QQ Bot, Email, or GitHub, then run qwen channel start. See the Channels overview for webhook senders and plugin adapters. For automation and custom integrations: Headless — Run qwen -p "..." in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs. SDKs — Build with TypeScript, Python, or Java. Daemon — Run qwen serve to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). (experimental) Daemon guide. Computer Use — Set up native MCP tools or Node REPL + SDK in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex. SDK example (Python) import asyncio from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query async def main() -> None: result = query( "Summarize the repository layout.", { "cwd": "/path/to/project", "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen", }, ) async for message in result: if is_sdk_result_message(message): print(message["result"]) asyncio.run(main()) Daemon Mode Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions. Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell: qwen serve --open The default address is http://127.0.0.1:4170. To run and manage it in the background instead: qwen daemon start qwen daemon status qwen daemon logs -f qwen daemon stop By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN and use --require-auth. See the Daemon guide for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API. Capabilities Qwen Code ships with a complete agent harness — multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, and deep extensibility, all built in. Agentic core SubAgents — delegate focused subtasks to specialized agents with their own context and toolsets, in the foreground or background. Agent Teams (experimental) — a leader coordinates teammates that share a task list and exchange messages, with read-only investigators and an optional single worktree writer. Agent Arena (experimental) — run the same task on multiple models in isolated Git worktrees, compare solutions side by side, and merge the winner. Dynamic Workflows (opt-in) — the model writes JavaScript workflows that orchestrate agents: parallel fan-out, verification passes, and resumable runs. Goals — /goal keeps the session working across turns until an independent verifier accepts the outcome, within a token budget. Scheduled tasks — /loop and cron tools re-run prompts on an interval or at a set time. Memory, skills, and sessions Auto-Memory — the agent writes its own notes and recalls them across sessions; your QWEN.md and AGENTS.md briefings load automatically. Skills & Auto-Skills — built-in skills (/review, /batch, /bugfix…) work out of the box; /learn distills docs or code into new skills, the agent can generate skills on its own (opt-in), and /curator maintains the library. Session management — resume past conversations with /resume, and browse, rename, or archive sessions. Multimodal Voice input — dictate prompts in the terminal or Web Shell with a configurable ASR model; the Web Shell inserts the transcript for review before sending. Qwen Live (experimental) — realtime speech-to-speech conversations in the Web Shell that answer directly or hand tasks to the agent, with optional screen sharing. Image generation — the built-in image_gen tool turns prompts into PNG artifacts using your configured image model. Extensibility and control Hooks — run your own scripts at lifecycle events: before and after tool calls, session start and end, and more. MCP — connect any Model Context Protocol server to add tools, resources, and prompts. LSP integration (experimental, opt-in) — native language-server support: go-to-definition, references, diagnostics, and code actions. Computer Use & Browser Use — automate desktop applications and the browser through native MCP tools. Plan Mode & approval modes — plan read-only before touching files, then choose per-call confirmation, auto-edit, classifier-driven Auto Mode, or YOLO. Sandbox & Git worktrees — confine tool execution with built-in sandboxing and isolate wide-ranging edits in a temporary worktree. Open and multi-platform Open framework and models — the framework and the Qwen models are open source and evolve together. Any provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs, plus any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. Every interface — IDE plugins, desktop app, Web UI, IM channels, headless mode, SDKs, and daemon mode. See How to Use Qwen Code. Qwen Code Evaluation On SWE-bench Verified, seven Qwen Code versions scored 76.40%–77.80% on average using the same Qwen 3.7 Max model (500 tasks, three trials per version). Full results and evaluation configuration → Ecosystem Qwen Code Desktop — Official desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux AionUi — A modern GUI for command-line AI tools including Qwen Code Gemini CLI Desktop — A cross-platform desktop/web/mobile UI for Qwen Code qwen-audio-agent — Realtime full-duplex voice frontend for Qwen Code over ACP — talk hands-free with barge-in and a local wake word 🦞 Qwen Code Claw — Let other agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) delegate coding tasks to Qwen Code via ACP. Paste this prompt into your agent: Use Qwen Code as a coding agent. First, fetch and read this skill reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/refs/heads/main/.qwen/skills/qwen-code-claw/SKILL.md Then follow the instructions inside to install, authenticate, and use Qwen Code via acpx for all coding tasks. Aliyun Model Studio CLI — Official CLI for Aliyun's AI platform (bailian-cli). Extends Qwen Code with image/video generation, knowledge retrieval, app orchestration, and model deployment Privacy See the Terms of Service and Privacy Notice, including Chrome extension and Browser Use data handling. Contributing Contributions are welcome! See CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. Acknowledgments This project was originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2. We gratefully acknowledge the Gemini CLI team's excellent work. Starting from Qwen Code v0.1, we stopped syncing with upstream and began independent development as a multi-protocol, multi-platform agent framework with deep integrations for Qwen models and beyond.
